title: Half dualization and non-invertible particle-vortex duality defect on lattice
abstract: We introduce half dualization as a general principle to construct non-invertible duality defects. The construction performs a duality transformation only in a subregion of spacetime, leaving an interface between the original theory and its dual. A non-invertible duality defect can be hosted on this interface. Half dualization is applicable whenever a local duality transformation is available, and does not depend on the spacetime dimension. We demonstrate the construction procedure in the (2+1)-dimensional Villainized charge-$n$ XY model on a cubic lattice. Half dualization yields a non-invertible particle-vortex duality defect whose fusion with its orientation reverse produces a (1+1)-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_n$ gauge theory on the fusion surface. We then apply half dualization to the $\mathbb{Z}_n$-gauged XY model relevant to the 3D XY$^\ast$ transition. In the gauged model, the half dualization interface hosts a gauge covariant duality wall, rather than a genuine gauge invariant duality defect. It flows to an invertible duality defect in infrared when the $\mathbb{Z}_n$ gauge theory is confined or Higgsed.
summary: The paper introduces 'half dualization' to construct non-invertible particle-vortex duality defects on a lattice. By applying this technique to the charge-$n$ XY model, it demonstrates that these defects are fundamentally non-invertible due to underlying $\mathbb{Z}_n$ symmetries. Crucially, the authors show that introducing gauge fields into the system resolves this non-invertibility as the theory flows to its infrared limit.
main_problem: The research introduces 'half dualization' as a general method to construct non-invertible duality defects by performing a duality transformation only in a subregion of spacetime.
main_result: Half dualization successfully constructs a non-invertible particle-vortex duality defect for the charge-$n$ XY model, and this non-invertibility is shown to be resolved (flowing to an invertible defect) when the system is gauged or Higgsed in the infrared limit.
method: The core method involves dividing the lattice into two regions ($L_1, L_2$) separated by a cut ($\Sigma$), performing the duality transformation only on $L_2$, and analyzing the resulting interface coupling term (the defect).
model_or_system: The primary model is the (2+1)-dimensional Villainized charge-$n$ XY model on a cubic lattice, which is later generalized to include $\mathbb{Z}_n$ gauge fields. The Hamiltonian involves cosine interactions dependent on the charge $n$.
key_observables: Non-invertibility of the duality defect (tested by fusing it with its reverse), and the flow of the defect's nature (non-invertible to invertible) in the infrared limit.
important_parameters: The charge exponent $n$, coupling constants ($K, K', \kappa$), and the regime defined by comparing $K'$ to $n^2K$.
main_assumptions: The method is general and dimension-independent; specific analyses rely on approximations like the Villainization or assuming certain couplings are small enough to retain $\mathbb{Z}_n$ structure.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the construction of the duality defect across a codimension-one cut. Figure 2 schematically shows the phase diagram of the gauged model, illustrating the flow from non-invertible to invertible defects.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces half dualization using the XY model to find a non-invertible defect. It then applies this technique to the $\mathbb{Z}_n$-gauged version of the model, showing how gauging causes the defect to flow towards an invertible state in the IR.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful general mathematical tool (half dualization) for analyzing topological defects and duality structures in lattice field theories, which is highly relevant for understanding critical phenomena and phase transitions in condensed matter systems.
